title: runtime digest depends on the reader's locale: one runtime reads 9f2c08f61dd5 under C and 74ca0ada3c39 under en_* UTF-8
body:
Found by dc on 2026-10-23 while recording 0201's rhad fixture, and confirmed by vc the same day.

`bin/devbin --version` reports one runtime under two identities, depending on the reader's collation. vc measured this in devbin's own checkout, on 0.1.12's runtime bytes:

- `LC_ALL=C`: `runtime 9f2c08f61dd5`
- `LC_ALL=C.UTF-8`: `runtime 9f2c08f61dd5`
- `LC_ALL=en_GB.UTF-8`: `runtime 74ca0ada3c39`
- `LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8`: `runtime 74ca0ada3c39`

dc measured the same in the 0201 fixture (vendored from the 0.1.12 keg) and in Utilz.

**Cause.** `runtime_digest` (lib/helpers:2557) lists lib's files and orders them with a bare `sort` (lib/helpers:2590). C collation puts `LICENSE.md` ahead of the lowercase names, and an en_* UTF-8 collation puts it among the l's. dc found that is the only difference in order across lib's files. Each path is part of the digested stream, so the digest follows the reader's `LC_COLLATE`. The comment above the function (lib/helpers:2548) left the sort alone "since a new order would change every install's digest", on the reading that the order was fixed. It is not fixed: it is whatever the reader's locale makes it.

**Why it matters.** The digest is the runtime's identity. `bin/devbin --version` reads it (version_identity, lib/helpers:2625), so does fleet's audit (bin/.devbin/cmd/fleet:185), and records compare it. The agent shell sets `LC_ALL=C`, hv's terminal is en_GB.UTF-8, and CI and kovacs set their own. So two readers of identical bytes record different identities. The 2026-10-17 sweep's "every runtime 74ca0ada3c39" was read under UTF-8, and an agent re-reading any of those estates today gets 9f2c08f61dd5, which reads as drift where there is none. The manifests are not affected (dc: byte-identical).

**Fix.** Pin the collation where the order is made: `LC_ALL=C sort` at lib/helpers:2590. The runtime already does this at its other ordering sorts (lib/release.steps, lib/infra.*, lib/cmd/clean, lib/install). Correct the comment at lib/helpers:2548 so it says why the order is pinned. The remaining unpinned sorts feed no digest, and the builder rules on each in the handover: bin/.devbin/cmd/fleet:1328 (a count of distinct states), bin/.devbin/cmd/fleet:1395 (a display order) and lib/release.notes:480 (`sort -V -r` over version strings). lib/install:559 is a comment.

**The arm.** In tests/unit/version.bats: one runtime's digest is the same under `LC_ALL=C` and under a UTF-8 locale whose collation differs from C's. The arm must first prove that the locale it names exists and really collates differently, eg by checking that `LICENSE.md` and a lowercase name sort in a different order under it. Otherwise it skips with the reason, because a runner without that locale falls back to C and would pass without testing anything. Red on main, green with the fix, under BSD and under GNU tools.

**Cost.** Every UTF-8 reader's digest moves once, to the value C readers already see. At 0.1.13 that costs nothing extra, because ST0008 WP-08 changes lib/ and moves every install's digest anyway.

Done when: runtime_digest orders lib's files the same under every locale; the arm is red on main under a collating UTF-8 locale and green with the fix, under BSD and GNU; the comment at lib/helpers:2548 says why the order is pinned; and the fix has landed in the 0.1.13 batch.

## Resolution

Fixed at 2f9c2618 in the 0.1.13 batch, on landing suite 20261023-2029 at 23f5f70e (2435 of 2435 ok, 5 skips, seal empty) (dc built it in a scratch clone of main at 358d3e7a; vc landed it).

- runtime_digest (lib/helpers) sorts lib's file list with `LC_ALL=C sort`, so the order of the paths in its stream, and so the digest, is the same under every locale. The comment above the function says why the order is pinned, and that a C reader's digest does not move while any other reader's moves once, to the C reader's.
- tests/unit/version.bats holds it: one runtime's digest under C equals its digest under en_US. It takes the locale from the harness's utf8_locale, plants a name C and en_US order apart, and proves the listing is the same lines in another order under that locale before comparing. Without such a locale, or where it orders as C does, it skips and says which. It is red on main ("one runtime has two digests: 4fb21ff0476f under C, d72f7b7f9e05 under en_US.UTF-8") and green at the fix, under BSD and GNU tools. On CI, the sibling arm built the same way runs on the Ubuntu and macOS legs and skips on the WSL leg, which has no en_US.UTF-8 (v0.1.12's run 39063041204).
- The other unpinned sorts feed no digest, and were measured under BSD and GNU sort, each in C, en_GB.UTF-8 and en_US.UTF-8, and left: fleet's snapshot comparison (bin/.devbin/cmd/fleet:1314-1318) compares two sets sorted under one collation; its count of distinct digests (:1328) and the order of its digest groups (:1395) are the same in every locale, and only the order of project names inside one group follows the reader, which is display; release.notes' version sort (lib/release.notes:480) reads only X.Y.Z. lib/install:559 is a comment.
